rules.title: Writ value grammar
rules.statement: value <- param_val / typed_value / typed_collection / map / array / STRING / FLOAT / INTEGER / TRUE / FALSE / NULL. The ordered alternation is the embeddable entry point for a Writ value; PEG ordering means earlier alternatives win (param_val, typed_value, and typed_collection are attempted before bare map/array/scalars).

rules.title: Scalar literal node codes
rules.statement: A bare STRING yields {CODE:STRING}, FLOAT yields {CODE:FLOAT}, INTEGER yields {CODE:INTEGER}, TRUE/FALSE yield {CODE:BOOLEAN, VALUE:true|false}, and NULL yields {CODE:NULL_VAL}. Boolean keywords carry the literal value; NULL carries no value.

rules.title: Map literal
rules.statement: map <- '{' (map_entry (',' map_entry)*)? ','? '}' producing {CODE:MAP, ITEMS:[...]}. The entry list may be empty and a single trailing comma is permitted after the last entry.

rules.title: Map entry key/value
rules.statement: map_entry <- (STRING / IDENT) ':' value producing {CODE:MAP_ENTRY, KEY, VALUE}. A key may be either a quoted STRING or a bare IDENT; the value is any Writ value.

rules.title: Array literal
rules.statement: array <- '[' (value (',' value)*)? ','? ']' producing {CODE:ARRAY, ITEMS:[...]}. The element list may be empty and a single trailing comma is permitted.

rules.title: Typed value constructor
rules.statement: typed_value <- datatype '(' value ')' producing {CODE:TYPED_VALUE, NAME:datatype, VALUE:value}. Exactly one inner value is wrapped by the named type constructor (e.g. Date("2026-01-01")).

rules.title: Typed array/map syntax hints
rules.statement: typed_collection <- typed_array / typed_map; typed_array <- '<' datatype '>' array; typed_map <- '<' datatype '>' map | '<' datatype ',' datatype '>' map. Type parameters preceding the collection are parse-time hints only: the parser still yields plain ARRAY/MAP nodes. A typed map may declare just the key type (value type defaults to AnyVal) or both key and value types.

rules.title: Datatype reference with generic args
rules.statement: datatype <- IDENT ('<' type_arg (',' type_arg)* '>')? producing {CODE:DATATYPE, NAME:IDENT, PARAMS:[...]}. The generic argument list, when '<...>' is present, must be non-empty.

rules.title: Generic type argument
rules.statement: type_arg <- datatype / INTEGER. A generic argument is either a nested datatype or a non-type integer literal (C++-style const generic argument).

rules.title: Positional parameter placeholder
rules.statement: param_val <- '$' INTEGER producing {CODE:PARAM_VAL, VALUE:INTEGER}. '$N' is a positional template parameter placeholder where N is a non-negative decimal integer (runtime type_hash=127, tag=0xFF).
